Nearest UNWORKED bid on the board (closed Aug 26). Pulled all 5 PDFs anonymously via the bidsandtenders preview route. Killed on three independent gates, any one of which is fatal. (1) Part B s6.0 Proposal Content: 'Proposals will be deemed complete if they include ALL of the following' and item (c) is 'a completed reference list. Proponents must provide three (3) appropriate references listing COMPLETED projects of a similar size and nature ... similar scope and value to that of the current Bid'. That is completeness, not scoring - a missing reference list makes the proposal incomplete. Reference-gated under Han's standing rule. (2) Part D (f) is worse and is a PRIOR-INSTALL gate: the three references must be 'for projects within the past five (5) years where the PROPOSED SOFTWARE has been implemented for at least one year' and 'comparable in size, scope, complexity, and relevance to municipal operations'. A product built for this bid cannot satisfy that by definition, at any quality level. (3) Scope is a 5-year COTS enterprise purchase (Price Schedule 1 = Yr1 setup+licence then Yr2-5 licence/subscription/maintenance) for Asset Management + Tangible Capital Asset (PSAB 3150) software, with a mandatory Functional Requirements Table whose Priority 1 items the City may use as a pass/fail cut, a 100-point live Product Demonstration of the existing product, and $2M per-claim / $4M aggregate Professional Liability Insurance. Submission is portal-only through the reCAPTCHA-gated bidsandtenders vendor account in any case.

KILL, reversing last run's 'this is the move'. Read all 12 pages. No disqualifier clause exists - and that was the wrong test. (1) s1.5: 'no contract will be awarded from the submissions received'; s1.1 makes any project contingent on Council endorsement and budget in EARLY 2027 with launch summer 2027; and s1.5 says a follow-on RFP will be 'open to all parties regardless of whether a response to this RFI has been submitted' with no obligation to notify respondents. A win pays nothing, in 2027, and confers no advantage. (2) s14 requires the Operator to run a customer call centre 7am-7pm Mon-Sat with 48h complaint resolution and a 3-level escalation ladder - headcount, not software. (3) s1.1 states demos are invited on 'proven experience working with Ontario municipalities' plus contactable references: the exact de facto gate that lost Vernon on 20 Aug. (4) 14 mandatory sections describe a mature paratransit platform (co-mingled dispatch, GTFS-RT connection protection, multi-tenant brokerage, volunteer mileage reimbursement, wheelchair capacity recalculation, inter-agency cost allocation with GIS jurisdiction tracking, PRESTO, driver MDT, GPS/IVR no-show workflow); s1.1 asks respondents to list what they cannot provide, which here is nearly the whole document. Also logged a DATE DISCREPANCY: PDF cover says closing 26 Aug 14:00, Bonfire portal field says 1 Sep 18:00Z - the portal is the submission mechanism and governs. Evidence and the generalisable rule ('zero disqualifiers' is necessary and badly insufficient - screen for what a WIN PAYS before screening for what could sink it) written to bonfire-sweep/BOARD.md.

KILL on Addendum II Q20, a written buyer refusal of exactly this portfolio's shape. Another proponent asked whether the City would review 'a proposal of a custom software build (designs & implementation plan) that meets ALL requirements in Appendix D ... We would need 2-3 weeks to build'. Answer: 'No, The City's is looking for a solution that is available and being used in the market and can demonstrate how it meets the City's requirements.' Supporting: Q19 makes prior-platform examples/customer references the scoring discriminator for Criterion 3 (Functionality, 20 pts, the largest non-price category), and Q18 requires the Stage III demo to run in the proponent's OWN SharePoint environment on their own release. What was NOT the problem, recorded so no future run re-litigates it: Addendum I Q2 explicitly waives SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / 3rd-party pen test as mandatory for Appendix F ('Evidence that verifies security controls is mandatory' instead) - the Vaughan/Mississauga clause family is genuinely absent here; Stage I is only 2 pass/fail items and Mandatory Technical Requirements is literally N/A; and the 65% cut is AGGREGATE over the five Stage II categories (48.75/75.00), not per-category, so scoring zero on References (10 pts) still ceilings at 87% and a pessimistic 5/15 Experience still lands 73%. The threshold was survivable; the COTS clause is not. TOOLING FINDING: screen-docs.mjs returned zero disqualifiers and was correct about the RFP body - the gate lives only in an addendum Q&A. Standing rule added to BOARD.md: screen addenda separately and read every Q&A answer even when the body is clean; a bid with unread addenda has not been screened. Both of this run's kills were invisible to a body-only read.

NOT the reason, and a reusable precedent: s4.9 insurance is 'should' not 'shall' AND names an alternative -- 'a letter signed by a licensed insurance broker stating that the Offeror is eligible to purchase the required insurance if the Offeror is selected'.
